Our Vision & Values
Ambition for All
We strive for excellence in everything we do. We set high expectations, nurture aspiration, and support every young person to achieve their full academic potential.
Building Confidence and Skills
We develop the knowledge, skills, and personal qualities students need to thrive in school, in society, and in life. We celebrate progress, encourage independence, and empower learners to believe in themselves.
Courage and Positivity to Be Better
We approach challenges with resilience, optimism, and determination. We show courage by learning from mistakes, embracing new opportunities, and taking pride in our efforts. We support one another with trust and respect so everyone feels they belong and can grow and improve every day.
Our Stories
Starting secondary school is a big milestone, and we're committed to making every step of the journey a positive one. From our Year 5 and 6 extra-curricular events and dedicated transition days to ongoing communication and support from our staff, we help every new student settle in with confidence, make new friends, and feel excited about their new chapter at Frogmore Community College. Thank you to our Year 7 parent for sharing such wonderful feedback – we're delighted to hear their son's transition has been such a positive experience. If you would like to find out more about joining Frogmore, we warmly welcome you to contact us to arrange a tour and meet with us. Please email admissions@frogmorecollege.co.uk. #frogmore #secondaryschool #year7 #yateley #hampshire
Yateley Town Council will be holding community litter picks on the following days during the half term holidays: 26th October 2026 10:00-11:30 at Yateley Green (meet in the Oak Room on the ground floor of our offices) 29th October 2026 11:00-12:30 at the Darby Green Centre All equipment is provided and children will need an adult with them to take part. Dogs on leads are very welcome! They will also have squash and maybe even some hot drinks for the adults! The council will also be holding their quarterly Community Climate Forum meeting from 19:00 on Monday 26th October in The Tythings. While this is aimed at adults, teenagers would be welcome to attend with a parent or guardian.
🗺️ What does it take to become a Geographer? 🌍 This half term, Year 7 have been finding out through their scheme of learning,‘What is a Geographer?’ Our students have been building the essential skills that create confident global explorers, including using Ordnance Survey maps, identifying map symbols and developing their grid-reference skills. These core skills provide an important foundation for future geographical learning, helping students become confident at interpreting and investigating the world around them. Year 7 have really embraced getting hands-on with their learning, working together to complete map challenges and putting their new skills into practice. 🌎🧭 #Year7Geography #Geography #MapSkills #GlobalExplorers #frogmorecommunitycollege #frogmore #yateley #hampshire #geography

Welcome
Welcome to Frogmore
As the new Principal of Frogmore from September 2026, it is a pleasure to warmly welcome you to our school website. Following a period of interim co-principal leadership, I am delighted to now take on the role of Principal and to lead Frogmore into this exciting next chapter. Frogmore is a warm, ambitious and forward-thinking school where our expert staff take the time to know every student as an individual. We are committed to delivering exceptional teaching in every lesson, every day.
This is an exciting moment in Frogmore’s journey. Since joining WMAT in 2024, Frogmore has embraced positive change to ensure we serve our community with the highest standards of education and care. I could not be prouder of the work ethic, resilience and commitment shown by our students, staff and families as we move forward with purpose and pace.
Frogmore is an inclusive school where academic excellence and character development are valued equally. Our mission is simple: to ensure every student leaves us with the qualifications, personal attributes, and confidence they need to thrive, both now and in the future, and to make a positive contribution to society.
We are a warm and welcoming community, and this website can only offer a glimpse of what makes Frogmore special. If you are a prospective family or a professional considering joining our team, we would be delighted to welcome you for a visit.
“Every Student. Every Potential. Every Success.”
At Frogmore, we are committed to equity, excellence, and the personal development of every student. Our dedicated staff take a genuine interest in each young person’s learning, wellâ€‘being, and aspirations, ensuring every individual is supported to achieve their full potential.
Ofsted captured this ethos during their visit in February 2022, awarding us a ‘Good’ judgement and noting:
“The school is a happy and friendly place to learn. Pupils say they feel that they belong.”
“They feel well supported and cared for by staff.”
We are proud members of the WMAT family, serving communities across Surrey and Hampshire. The Trust also includes the i2i SCITT, enabling us to train and develop Early Career Teachers in-house.
Since joining WMAT, we have:
Looking ahead we are excited about the future of Frogmore. Our ongoing development plans include:
Our staff collaborate twice weekly in carefully designed professional development sessions to ensure our teaching is inclusive, research informed, and responsive to students’ needs. Key subject areas benefit from Trust Directors who coach and support teams, ensuring we draw on the full strength of WMAT expertise.
Our students are the best ambassadors for Frogmore. They speak passionately about the care, opportunities, and high quality teaching they receive every day. Attendance is strong and students enjoy a wealth of extra-curricular opportunities, including long established clubs, new initiatives, and the Duke of Edinburgh Award from Year 9.
Choosing a school, or a place to work, is an important decision. I warmly encourage you to visit us, experience our vibrant daily life, and see for yourself what makes Frogmore such a special community. I am confident you will be impressed, and we look forward to meeting you.
Principal, from September 2026

Home Learning Club
To support students with their Home Learning, we run a free supervised Home Learning Club in the Learning Resource Centre (LRC) from Monday to Thursday each week from 15:05 - 16:00. This provides a calm, focused space where students can complete their work, with access to computers and other resources as needed. There is no need for students to prebook for this club.
If a student does not meet the required standards and deadline for home learning without good reason, they may be expected to attend a home learning support session after school. If they fail to attend the support session, a sanction will be applied in line with the behaviour policy.

Enrichment & Extra Curricular
Friends and Belonging
Building friendships is an essential life skill and a big part of settling into secondary school. From the very first day, we support students in getting to know one another by carefully allocating tutor groups and running welcoming activities within them. These early opportunities help students feel comfortable and begin forming positive relationships.
There are many ways for students to make new friends, joining a lunchtime or after-school club is a great place to start. And if your child notices someone on their own, we always encourage a simple "hello", because sometimes the smallest gesture can lead to a great friendship.
Extra-curricular activities: sports teams and school fixtures
Frogmore offers a range of lunchtime and after-school extra-curricular activities to students. These include both sporting and non-sporting clubs designed to enrich your child’s school experience and encourage them to try new interests.
School Trips and Educational Experiences
We organise a range of educational visits and school trips throughout the year. These experiences:
We always aim to give parents plenty of notice about upcoming trips, including all necessary details and deadlines. Please note:
We warmly encourage all students to participate and enjoy the fantastic opportunities available beyond the classroom at Frogmore.

Careers Programme
SLT Line Manager - Grant Davies
Careers Leader - Victoria Delehanty
Careers Advisor – Lorna Durbridge
At Frogmore, we believe that every child can excel. The aim of our curriculum is to inspire and empower every child, through rich and memorable experiences, to flourish in their learning and live a fulfilled life, confidently equipped with breadth and depth of knowledge to play an active and informed role in society. Providing a robust Careers Information, Advice and Guidance (CIAG) programme for our students is an important part of this commitment.
The Careers Curriculum
We are committed to exploring how the subjects that we offer can prepare students for life after Frogmore and we make explicit links to careers in our lessons. In addition to this, age appropriate careers- related PSHCE lessons are delivered to all students.
Towards the end of Key Stage 3, students are invited, along with their parents, to a Key Stage 4 options evening where they look into the different subjects that they can take, whether they be GCSEs or vocational qualifications. Following this, students have one- to-one bespoke careers guidance meetings about their option choices.
In key stage 4, students undertake a variety of activities to prepare them for life beyond Frogmore. Each student has a post-16 options advice and guidance interview with our careers advisor, Lorna Durbridge from Sixth Form College Farnborough. All students are offered an appointment but they can also request an appointment by speaking to Mr Davies, Mrs Delehanty, their Director of Year or their tutor.
In addition, we offer the following opportunities:
Our careers advisor is in school every Thursday and based in Mr Davies’ office.
During student career appointment, the careers advisor will help students to think about their future, what interests them, what college courses they would like to do after they leave Frogmore, as well as possible university options or future careers.
Interview sessions are 50 minutes long, after which, students are able to email the careers advisor directly with any questions they might have or for follow up information. Students will also receive an action plan from the session, as well as web links and additional information to help guide them via their school email
Impact of careers programme
We measure the impact of the school’s career programme through the DFE published Destination Data.
